title: Gold heads for its biggest yearly drop in 11 years as the Iran war lifts yields and the dollar
body: The poll shows the gold outlook is being driven by the Iran war's knock-on effects rather than by safe-haven buying. Higher oil prices have fed through to yields, the dollar and expectations that rates will stay high, which raises the cost of holding bullion. That makes crude a key upstream driver for gold: any easing in oil and yields, for example on progress in US-Iran talks, would remove one of the main headwinds analysts cite. Silver carries extra downside risk because its industrial exposure leaves it vulnerable to softer solar demand on top of the rate pressure. The forecast gap between the two metals favours gold over silver. --- Earlier: UBS sees limited gold downside as three demand pillars set a floor near $4,000 --- The Iran war has turned gold's usual crisis logic on its head, with oil-driven yields and a firm dollar doing the damage, but analysts are betting central banks will catch it on the way down.

title: Strategy's bitcoin buying hinges on one number: STRC at $100
body: What is happening Strategy, the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, bought no bitcoin in the week of October 19 to 25. Instead it spent $204.9 million buying back its own STRC preferred shares, according to its October 26 filing with the SEC. Those buybacks have helped lift STRC to about $99.36, its highest level in roughly five months and just shy of its $100 par value. Social media accounts have run with the next step: Michael Saylor is "set to resume heavy Bitcoin buying" once STRC gets back to $100. That claim rests on a real, stated plan. Whether it plays out as "heavy" is a different question, and readers may get some answers soon. Strategy reports third-quarter results after the US close on Thursday, October 29, with a webinar at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time. What STRC is and why $100 matters STRC, nicknamed Stretch, is a perpetual preferred share with a variable dividend that Strategy pays monthly. The dividend is adjusted to keep the price anchored near its $100 par value, and Strategy raised the rate to 12% during the summer slump. The $100 level matters because Strategy has said it will not sell new STRC below par. Above it, STRC becomes a fundraising tool again: Strategy can sell shares into the market and use the cash to buy bitcoin. It still has about $17.5 billion of STRC available to sell under its at-the-market (ATM) programme, and that figure has not moved in its weekly filings since at least June. Management has been explicit about the link.

title: Recap: Fed holds at 3.75%-4% in 10-2 vote as Cook dissents for a hike, December move in focus
body: A hold with two hawkish dissents and no pushback from Warsh on December pricing keeps the bias firmly toward tightening, which supports Treasury yields and the dollar into year end. Cook's dissent matters for rate expectations because it widens hawkish support beyond the committee's usual hard-liners, strengthening the case that a December hike has broad backing. The dissent may also be read politically, given Trump's efforts to remove her, which adds to scrutiny of Fed independence. Fewer scheduled rate decisions from next year mean each meeting carries more weight, and that could amplify market moves around those dates. --- Earlier: investingLive Americas FX news wrap 28 Oct: Fed holds rates, yield curve steepens as Big Tech earnings diverge --- The Fed paused, but with two votes for a hike and a chair insisting the job isn't done, the pause looks more like a breather than a turn.

title: NZX 50 Edges Higher, Attempts to Extend Gains
body: The NZX 50 rose 25 points, or 0.2%, to 13,716 in Thursday morning trading, extending a modest gain from the previous session as both the RBNZ and the Federal Reserve kept interest rates on hold. Upside momentum was limited, however, as traders remained cautious in the wake of the RBNZ's latest decision and growing signals that a rate hike is possible at the next meeting, with higher oil prices adding to inflation risks. On Tuesday, the central bank unexpectedly left the official cash rate unchanged at 2.75% in a split decision, while signalling that further tightening remains on the table to contain rising inflation. Sentiment was also restrained ahead of business confidence figures due later today, after September's reading fell to a three‑month low. Sector-wise, energy, healthcare, and real estate led the advance. Notable early movers included Freightways Group (up 2.8%), Channel Infrastructure (0.9%), Fisher & Paykel Healthcare (0.6%), Infratil (0.6%), and A2 Milk (0.5%). title: South Korea's Manufacturing Sentiment Weakens Slightly
body: South Korea's manufacturing Business Survey Index slipped to 78 in October 2026 from 79 in September, signaling a further weakening in business conditions. In contrast, the financial situation index edged up to 83 from 81, while the inventories index declined to 97 from 103. At the same time, the Composite Business Sentiment Index rose to 105.6 from 99.5, indicating broader improvements in other components. The production index increased to 94 from 89, and the new orders index advanced to 91 from 84. The Composite Business Sentiment Index for the outlook for the following month also strengthened, gaining 1.9 points to reach 103.0. title: South Korea's Manufacturing Sentiment Slips in November, Underscoring Fragile Industry Outlook
body: South Korea's Manufacturing Business Survey Index (BSI) edged down in November, signaling a slight deterioration in sentiment among industrial firms. The indicator stood at 78 in November 2025, slipping from a level of 79 recorded in July 2026, according to data updated on 28 October 2026. While the change is marginal, the sub-80 reading indicates that pessimists continue to outnumber optimists in the manufacturing sector. The modest decline suggests that manufacturers remain cautious about demand, costs, and overall business conditions, with no clear sign yet of a decisive improvement in the operating environment. The updated figures highlight the ongoing fragility of South Korea's industrial recovery path. Investors and policymakers are likely to watch upcoming BSI releases closely for confirmation of whether this softening in confidence is temporary or the start of a more prolonged downturn in manufacturing sentiment. title: TSX Edges Higher After BoC and US Fed Meetings
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index finished 0.3% higher at 36,265 on Wednesday after the Bank of Canada raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 2.5%, in line with expectations. The central bank said the hike is intended to limit the risk that persistently elevated energy prices spill over into broader goods and services inflation, and signaled that further rate increases may be required. By contrast, the US Federal Reserve left its policy rate unchanged, also as anticipated. Financial shares were generally stronger, with BMO and CIBC each advancing 0.6%. In the mining sector, several companies were set to report earnings after the close. Agnico Eagle gained 0.9% and Alamos rose 1.3%, while Kinross slipped 0.4% and First Quantum declined 0.5%. Teck Resources added 0.7% ahead of its results due Thursday, while Imperial Oil climbed 1.1% and Cameco advanced 1.3% before their scheduled reports on Friday. Among energy names, Tamarack Valley inched up 0.1% after lifting its 2026 production forecast, and Trican Well Service rose 0.7% on the back of stronger third-quarter profit. title: Ibovespa Hits Two-Month Low
body: The Ibovespa dropped almost 2.6% on Wednesday to close at 171,006, marking its third consecutive decline and the lowest level in roughly two months. Investors remained focused on the implications of President Lula's election victory, amid mounting fiscal concerns and uncertainty surrounding the makeup of his economic team. Banking shares were among the hardest hit. Santander sank 5% after reporting a 28% year-on-year decline in recurring managerial net income. Other major financial names also retreated: Bradesco fell 6.7%, Itaú slid 3.4%, Itaúsa lost 2.9%, Banco do Brasil dropped 3.2%, and B3 declined 5.1%. Utilities weakened as well, with Axia down 5.2%. In the corporate spotlight, Ambev slipped 2.2% and Vale retreated 3% ahead of their earnings releases scheduled for Thursday. Petrobras eased 0.5% despite a rebound in international oil prices. On the external front, the US Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged, in line with market expectations. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Wall Street Rises as Fed Holds Rates Steady
body: US stock indices closed higher on Wednesday, with the S&P 500 up 0.3%, the Nasdaq gaining 0.2%, and the Dow edging just above the flatline, as investors absorbed the latest FOMC decision and remarks from Fed Chair Warsh. As widely anticipated, the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged, though two policymakers dissented in favor of a 25 bps hike. Warsh struck a confident tone on inflation, indicating that inflation expectations remain well anchored. Financial heavyweights generally advanced, with JPMorgan up 1%, Morgan Stanley rising 1.7%, Goldman Sachs gaining 1.5%, and Wells Fargo adding 1.2%. Corporate earnings remained a key driver, with Microsoft (-0.1%) and Alphabet (+1.3%) scheduled to report after the close. Alphabet also gained support from reports that OpenAI plans to purchase AI computing chips from Google. Record quarterly profits at SK Hynix boosted semiconductor shares, lifting Micron (+5.9%) and AMD (+3.2%). By contrast, Apple slipped 0.9% despite unveiling a revamped MacBook Pro equipped with a touchscreen. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com
